newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly gain ground with gas, cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly gain ground with gas, cold.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly gained ground again Friday in moderate trade, helped by still-firm natgas prices and forecasts for below-normal East Coast weather next week, industry sources said.

"Unless crude or gas gives up, resid sellers aren't giving anything away," said one cash trader, noting high gas prices recently prompted many utilities to switch to cheaper resid. In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained a quarter to $22.25-50 a barrel, while December paper was talked slightly higher at $22.25-50, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour firmed more than 25 cents to the $22.75 area, with Jan HP paper reportedly bid at $24.20.
High sulphurs in NYH held relatively steady. NYH Dec 2.2 percent paper was talked at $20.00-50.
U.S. Gulf one percent jumped almost $1 to $19.75 on tighter supplies as shippers fixed barrels for the East Coast.
"There are quite a few barrels from the Gulf headed East," said one trader.
USG three percent gained 50 cents to $18.25-50 on reports 50,000 barrels of prompt HSFO sold at $18.50.

New York City gate swing gas held relatively steady Friday in the mid-$4.50s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was quoted at $5.00-5.15/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent.
Bids are due Tuesday for a Midwest utility tender for 0.7 percent material for December delivery.
There was no word on Friday's New York utility tender for 100,000 barrels of 1.5 percent for 12/20 delivery.
